questions.stem: Which inequality represents the half-plane to the right of the line x = 2?
questions.solution: The line x = 2 divides the plane into two half-planes: one to the left (x < 2) and one to the right (x > 2). The inequality x > 2 represents the half-plane to the right of the line.
questions.explanation: To identify the half-plane, consider which side of the line the inequality allows for. In this case, x > 2 means that x can take any value greater than 2, which is on the right side of the line.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose 'B', as it represents the half-plane to the left of the line.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents the half-plane above the line y = -3x?
questions.solution: The line y = -3x divides the plane into two half-planes: one below (y < -3x) and one above (y > -3x). The inequality y > -3x represents the half-plane above the line.
questions.explanation: To identify the half-plane, consider which side of the line the inequality allows for. In this case, y > -3x means that y can take any value greater than the corresponding value of -3x, which is on the upper side of the line.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake would be to choose 'B', as it represents the half-plane below the line.
